The WHO/UNAIDS/UNICEF-recommended replacement milks for infants of HIV-infected mothers are generally appropriate in the South African context, but with some considerations. 

In South Africa, the recommended replacement milks are usually infant formula. However, the use of infant formula in this context requires access to clean water and proper preparation to minimize the risk of waterborne illnesses. Additionally, the cost of infant formula can be a significant burden for many families in South Africa.

The South African Department of Health recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months, unless the mother is HIV-positive and not on antiretroviral therapy (ART), in which case replacement feeding with infant formula is advised if it is acceptable, feasible, affordable, sustainable, and safe (AFASS).

Overall, while the recommended replacement milks are appropriate in the South African context, it is crucial to consider the individual circumstances of each mother and infant, including access to resources, support, and healthcare services.
